task.instruction: Grade one Claude Code skill folder against the owner's ask: given a target, the skill finds the target's subject, derives a rubric, actually grades the target and writes a graded HTML report. Judge from the folder's files alone.

world.scope: one skill folder: SKILL.md, references, scripts, assets and examples at one commit
world.deliverable: a pass or fail per criterion for the folder, read by the plugin owner

task.evidence_goal: the grade shows whether the folder does the four steps, ends in a graded HTML report, and is built to report and grade reliably

tiers.name: the owner's ask: name, four steps and the HTML report

criteria.text: The skill folder is named card and its SKILL.md front matter has name: card, with no skill folder named rubric beside it.
variants_ok: skills/card/SKILL.md with name: card; no skills/rubric folder.
near_miss: skills/review/SKILL.md with name: review.
skills/card/ exists but skills/rubric/ is also still there.

provenance.source: https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1046 DECIDED: owner said: name it card, not review

criteria.text: SKILL.md or a reference it routes to has a step that makes the agent write down the target's subject: what the target is, what it is for, who reads or uses it.
criteria.anchors: Subject means those three facts about the target; the step must name all three, and must come before the step that derives criteria.
variants_ok: A Profile step that writes genre, purpose and reader into a file before criteria.
A step that asks the agent to fill a three-field subject record.
near_miss: A step that only asks the agent to read the target.
A step naming purpose but not the reader.

provenance.source: https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1046 owner verbatim: 주제가 무엇인지 파악하고

criteria.text: A step derives the rubric from the written subject, so the criteria depend on what the target is for and who reads it.
criteria.anchors: Derived from the subject means the step names the subject record as its input; a fixed list of criteria used for every target does not count.
variants_ok: Derive step: input is the profile; output is a rubric spec file.
The step picks a framework menu for the genre, then instantiates it per target.
near_miss: A fixed checklist applied to any target with no subject input.

provenance.source: https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1046 owner verbatim: 그것의 rubric을 도출해서

criteria.text: A step grades the target itself against the derived rubric and records one verdict per criterion.
criteria.anchors: Actually grading means the skill's own steps produce verdicts on the target; telling the person how they could grade does not count.
variants_ok: A Grade step that hands the target and rubric to a judge, which returns a verdict per criterion.
A script that scores a verdict file the Grade step produced.
near_miss: The skill ends with a rubric and tells the person to grade later.
The skill only measures how well a rubric agrees with human labels.

provenance.source: https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1046 owner verbatim: 실제로 평가하고

criteria.text: The skill's final output is a graded HTML report file, and a step names that file as the deliverable.
criteria.anchors: Graded means the page shows the verdicts from the Grade step, not only the rubric.
variants_ok: A Report step that writes report.html from the verdicts via a script or a template.
An assets/ page template filled with the verdicts.
near_miss: The final output is a JSON spec.
The report is Markdown.
The HTML shows the rubric with no verdicts.

provenance.source: https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1046 owner verbatim: 그것으로 평가된 html report를 만드는 것

criteria.text: The skill builds its HTML by a script or a template kept in its own folder, with a finished sample report in examples/, as a skill that shows its output in HTML does.
variants_ok: scripts/render-report.py plus examples/sample-report.html.
assets/report.html template plus examples/ sample.
near_miss: The agent is told to write HTML freehand each time with no template and no sample.

provenance.source: https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1046 owner verbatim: zoom, book, tree가 html로 보여주는 것처럼; AGENTS.md Skill folders

criteria.text: The skill's steps end with a rubric or spec file and name no step that grades the target or writes a report.
criteria.anchors: Grading the target means producing verdicts on the target; scoring sample answers only to test a spec does not count as grading the target.
variants_ok: A Grade step and a Report step exist after Derive.
near_miss: Steps: Frame, Criteria, Tiers, Weights, Calibrate, end.

provenance.source: the old rubric skill, which authors, calibrates and repairs specs but does not grade a given target; https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1046

criteria.text: The report spec puts a verdict and a fix list for the failed criteria before any per-criterion detail.
criteria.anchors: Before detail means earlier in the page order the skill prescribes than the criterion cards.
variants_ok: Layout: header, verdict, fix first, tier bars, cards.
Fix list sits right under the verdict.
near_miss: Layout opens with the full criterion table and puts fixes last.

provenance.source: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/inverted-pyramid/ ; research-report.md rules 1 and 3

criteria.text: The report layout leads with one blended score, such as a percentage or an average over all criteria, as its headline.
criteria.anchors: Blended means one number that mixes criteria of different tiers. A count for each tier, or a tier statement such as tier 2 not met, is not blended.
variants_ok: Headline is the highest tier fully passed with pass counts for each tier.
near_miss: Headline reads 78/100.

provenance.source: https://github.com/ossf/scorecard says the aggregate hides individual behaviours; research-report.md rule 2

criteria.text: The grading step makes the judge quote evidence from the target, with a file or line or an excerpt, before it gives each verdict.
criteria.anchors: Before means the output field order or the instruction order puts the quote first.
variants_ok: Judge output per criterion: quote, then met 0 or 1.
Evidence field required; empty means not met.
near_miss: The judge returns only a pass or fail per criterion.

provenance.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.08654 RULERS; https://arxiv.org/html/2306.05685 chain of thought; research-rubric.md rule 8

criteria.text: The grading step counts a verdict that has no quoted evidence as not met.
variants_ok: A script that rejects or zeroes a verdict whose evidence is empty.
near_miss: A verdict with empty evidence is accepted as given.

provenance.source: research-rubric.md rule 8 (RULERS evidence-grounded)

criteria.text: The grading step runs the judge as a fresh subagent that receives only the target and the frozen rubric.
criteria.anchors: Fresh means a new context that holds none of the conversation that wrote or revised the target.
variants_ok: A brief to a new subagent that lists the target path and the rubric path only.
near_miss: The same session that wrote the target grades it.
The judge brief includes the author's opinion of the target.

provenance.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.13076 self-preference; https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.04549 shared context; research-rubric.md rule 10

criteria.text: The skill writes the rubric to a file before grading starts, and says a change after grading is logged as a new version.
variants_ok: Rubric saved with a hash, graded from that file.
A rubric version number bumps on every edit after grading.
near_miss: The rubric is held in chat and may be edited while grading.

provenance.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.08654 RULERS locked rubric; https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.12272 criteria drift; research-rubric.md rule 7

criteria.text: The report spec requires each failed criterion to show the criterion, the quoted evidence, why it fails and a fix.
criteria.anchors: Four named fields; a card that lacks any of them does not meet it.
variants_ok: Card fields: criterion, evidence, reason, fix.
near_miss: Card shows only the criterion and a red mark.

provenance.source: https://www.cultofpedagogy.com/single-point-rubric/ ; research-report.md rule 3

criteria.text: The report spec marks pass and fail with an icon or a word as well as colour.
variants_ok: Each status shows a check mark and the word Met, plus a colour.
A page template where every status cell carries text.
near_miss: Green and red fills with no text or icon.

provenance.source: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html WCAG 1.4.1

criteria.text: The report spec has a separate section for criteria that could not be judged, each with its reason, kept out of the pass and fail counts.
variants_ok: A Not judged section that lists reason per criterion.
near_miss: An unjudged criterion counts as failed.

provenance.source: https://github.com/ossf/scorecard unscorable checks; https://github.com/GoogleChrome/lighthouse/blob/main/docs/understanding-results.md notApplicable

tiers.name: skill craft from AGENTS.md and Anthropic practices

criteria.text: The SKILL.md description begins with Use when and is at most 300 characters.
variants_ok: description: Use when a target needs a graded report. Not for X.
near_miss: description: Grades things.
A description in the first person.

provenance.source: AGENTS.md Skills: Description; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices

criteria.text: SKILL.md holds a routing table that sends each case to one file under references/ named after the case.
criteria.anchors: Each case means each mode of the skill, such as profile, derive, grade or report.
variants_ok: Table rows: case, reference file.
near_miss: SKILL.md holds every step inline with no references/.

provenance.source: AGENTS.md Skills: Routing table

criteria.text: Counting, scoring and building the report page are done by a script in scripts/ named verb-noun.py, not by prose.
variants_ok: scripts/score-verdicts.py and scripts/build-report.py.
near_miss: Prose tells the agent to add up the verdicts by hand.
scripts/report.py

provenance.source: AGENTS.md Skills: Code computes; Plugin layout: Names

criteria.text: The skill folder holds no agents/, tests/ or evals/ folder.
variants_ok: Folder has SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, assets/, examples/.
near_miss: An agents/judge.md file.

provenance.source: AGENTS.md Plugin layout: No agents, No tests or evals

criteria.text: SKILL.md is under 500 lines, and every reference file is linked directly from SKILL.md, not through another reference.
variants_ok: SKILL.md of 90 lines linking all references.
near_miss: A reference file that only another reference links to.

provenance.source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices body under 500 lines; references one level deep
